the following decision problems are NP-complete: (1) given a graph and a set of vertices to be colored, decide if there is an acyclic coloring of the vertices, where the vertices are colored in such a way that no two vertices with an edge between them have the same color; (2) given a graph, a set of vertices, and a set of edges between these vertices, decide if there exists a coloring of the vertices that is acyclic and respects the edges.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the algorithms presented in this thesis can be used for on-line seat reservation problems, and the algorithms can be applied in a wide range of problems.
we present a new class of problems that we call on-line off-line scheduling, and develop algorithms with optimal time complexity to handle problems of that nature.
we have developed algorithms with optimal running times for the problems of deciding if it is safe to reserve a seat in a train, or a plane, or a theatre, and, if so, how to do it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we develop algorithms with optimal time for on-line problems, and for off-line problems with optimal time, we develop algorithms with the same running time, or with a constant factor worse running time, but with optimal approximation ratio.
we show that it is possible to solve the off-line problems in time linear in the number of passengers and the number of trains, and in polynomial time in the number of seats per train.
we develop optimal algorithms for a number of problems in the area of on-line and off-line seat reservations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the off-line problem is not harder than the on-line one.
the on-line problem is easier than the off-line one.
the running time for on-line problems can often be improved when the on-line problem is embedded into an off-line one.
